name: PCA9685PW,118
title: PCA9685: 16-channel, 12-bit PWM Fm+ I2C-bus LED controller
summary: Sixteen PWM outputs controlled over a 1 MHz Fast-mode Plus I2C bus. Each output has its own 12-bit on and off points within a shared period, so both brightness and turn-on phase are set per channel; one prescaler sets the frequency from about 24 Hz to 1526 Hz off a 25 MHz internal oscillator or an external clock up to 50 MHz. Outputs sink 25 mA (totem pole also sources 10 mA) at 5 V and tolerate 5.5 V; an active-LOW OE pin gates them all. Six address pins allow 62 devices on one bus. It runs from 2.3 V to 5.5 V over -40 °C to +85 °C in TSSOP28 or HVQFN28.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: A bus master drives SDA, SCL and OE with pull-ups to VDD. A0, A2 and A4 are tied high and A1, A3, A5 low, giving the bus address 1010 101x; EXTCLK is grounded so the internal oscillator runs. Each group of four outputs drives four N-channel MOSFETs: two switch a single 5 V LED each, one switches three 5 V LEDs in parallel, and one switches a string of three LEDs from 12 V. MODE2 is set to INVRT = 0, OUTDRV = 1, OUTNE = 01.

equations.note: 25 MHz and 200 Hz give 30 (1Eh), the reset value. The hardware will not accept a value below 3. 03h gives 1526 Hz, FFh gives 24 Hz.

where.EXTCLK: frequency on the EXTCLK pin, DC to 50 MHz

operation.text: Sixteen outputs, each with its own 12-bit PWM (4096 steps, 0 % to 100 % duty); all share one frequency, about 24 Hz to 1526 Hz. Outputs are totem pole by default (25 mA sink, 10 mA source at 5 V) or open-drain by software (25 mA sink at 5 V); all 16 take the same type. Inputs and outputs tolerate 5.5 V. LEDs up to 25 mA and 5.5 V connect straight to a pin; heavier or higher-voltage loads need an external driver. At power-on the outputs are LOW.

I2C-bus slave up to Fast-mode Plus (1 MHz), with a 30 mA SDA output for heavily loaded buses (up to 4000 pF). SDA and SCL have spike filters. Hot insertion is supported. A LOW lasting 25 ms or more on SDA or SCL resets the bus interface.

Runs from 2.3 V to 5.5 V over -40 °C to +85 °C, with 5.5 V tolerant inputs, an internal power-on reset and low standby current. The 25 MHz oscillator needs no external parts. ESD protection exceeds 2000 V HBM (JESD22-A114), 200 V MM (JESD22-A115) and 1000 V CDM (JESD22-C101); latch-up tested to JESD78 beyond 100 mA.

The address byte is 1 A5 A4 A3 A2 A1 A0 R/W; the six address pins have no pull-ups and must be strapped. Of 64 codes, the LED All Call (1110 000) and Software Reset (0000 0110) addresses are live at power-up, leaving 62. Also avoid the PCA9564 (0000 000) and PCA9665 (1110 000) master addresses, the reserved codes 0000 011 and 1111 1XX, 10-bit addressing (1111 0XX), the General Call (0000 000) and the Hs-mode master code (0000 1XX) where other devices could see them; in a closed system they work as ordinary addresses.

operation.topic: All Call and Sub Call addresses
operation.text: ALLCALLADR resets to E0h (1110 000X) and is enabled at power-up, so every PCA9685 acknowledges E0h/E1h; do not use it as an individual address. SUBADR1-3 reset to E2h, E4h and E8h and are disabled until the matching SUBx bit in MODE1 is set, so they may serve as ordinary addresses while disabled. All four are volatile, rewritable over the bus, usable for reads and writes; only bits 7:1 count and bit 0 reads 0.

Send START, the General Call address 00h with R/W = 0, then the single data byte 06h, then STOP. The part acknowledges only that address and only 06h, and acknowledges no further bytes. On the STOP it returns to its power-up state and is addressable again after tBUF. A NACK at any point means the reset was aborted and no registers changed. It needs a working bus with no device holding it.

After an address is acknowledged, the next byte goes into the control register (reset 00h), which points at the register to access. With MODE1 AI = 1 the pointer steps after each byte, wrapping from register 69 to 0, and from 254 back to 0 when started at 250. A software reset call uses no control byte.

MODE1 SLEEP is 1 after reset, so the 25 MHz oscillator is off and no output can switch, dim or blink until SLEEP is cleared. The oscillator needs up to 500 µs to start after SLEEP goes to 0. PRE_SCALE can be written only while SLEEP = 1. If every output is set full OFF, the prescaler and PWM timing logic stop.

To change over to EXTCLK: set SLEEP, then write 1 to both SLEEP and EXTCLK. The external clock may already run, since the chip is asleep. EXTCLK then stays set until power is cycled or a software reset is sent. No start-up wait applies with an external clock. Several devices on one clock run in step. Ground EXTCLK when unused.

Sleeping with PWM channels still running sets RESTART once the current PWM cycle finishes and holds all PWM registers. To resume: read MODE1, and if RESTART is 1 clear SLEEP, wait 500 µs, then write 1 to RESTART; every channel restarts and RESTART clears. SLEEP must have been 0 for at least 500 µs first. RESTART also clears on power cycle, software reset, writing any PWM register followed by STOP (OCH = 0), or a write to all four registers of a channel (OCH = 1). Turning every channel off before sleeping (ALL_LED_OFF_H bit 4, or bit 4 of each LEDn_OFF_H) also clears RESTART, and the PWM registers must then be reloaded.

A 12-bit counter runs 0 to 4095 each PWM period. Each output has a 12-bit ON count and a 12-bit OFF count: the output asserts when the counter matches ON and negates when it matches OFF, so both the delay and the duty are set in steps of 1/4096 of the period. ON and OFF should never hold the same value. For a 10 % delay and 20 % duty: ON = 409 (199h), OFF = 409 + 819 = 1228 (4CCh). For 90 % delay and 90 % duty the OFF point wraps: ON = 3685 (E65h), OFF = 3685 + 3686 - 4096 = 3275 (CCBh). New values load when the LOW part of a cycle ends so no glitch is seen.

Bit 4 of LEDn_ON_H set: output always on, turning on after the ON delay, and the OFF count is ignored. Bit 4 of LEDn_OFF_H set: output always off, ON count ignored. If both are set, full off wins. Every output resets with full OFF set. ALL_LED_ON and ALL_LED_OFF (FAh to FDh) write the same values into every channel in four bytes; they read back as zero.

With OCH = 0 (default) the outputs change at the STOP, so one or more PWM registers of 06h to 45h may be loaded in any sequence and change together, and several devices can be synchronised. With OCH = 1 a channel changes on the ACK of the last of its four PWM registers, and only once all four are written.

OE LOW: outputs follow their PWM registers with the polarity set by INVRT. OE HIGH: outputs go to 0, 1 or high-impedance as OUTNE[1:0] selects. OE can blink several devices together from one external clock, or dim them by being pulsed fast enough not to be seen, its duty setting brightness.

An internal reset holds the chip until VDD reaches VPOR, then loads all registers and the bus state machine with defaults. To reset again VDD must fall below 0.2 V. No glitches appear on the outputs at power-up.

INVRT keeps firmware the same whichever driver is used, flipping output polarity while OE = 0. OUTDRV picks totem pole or open-drain to cut external parts. Best settings: direct LEDs to VDD through a resistor, INVRT = 1 with OUTDRV = 0; N-type driver, INVRT = 0 with OUTDRV = 1; P-type driver, INVRT = 1 with OUTDRV = 1.
Use open-drain mode. In totem-pole mode the Zener gives a low-resistance path from the output to ground and the IC overheats.

Edge control mainly slows output turn-on; turn-off is fast, about 1.5 ns. Simulated open-drain turn-on is about 14 ns at VDD = 3.6 V, CL = 50 pF, RPU = 500 Ω. Open-drain mode suits direct LED drive where ISS and ground bounce matter. Switching all 16 outputs at 25 mA can bounce ground; about 50 pF of decoupling is on chip, and more may be added externally as close to the part as possible.
The single ground pin carries up to 400 mA; two die ground pads bond to it. Some ground bounce may occur without upsetting operation, and external decoupling lowers it.
The die ground connects to both the VSS pin and the exposed pad. VSS must be grounded. The pad should be soldered to a board thermal pad with thermal vias under it.
